claim: FC-R06 / ERP_RIDER_SHARE give RydeFLASH the full share 1.0 whenever the carpool status is not recorded, although Ryde's own article ties RydeFLASH to carpool drivers, for whom the rider owes only 50%. The ontology declares is_carpool a data gap (absent from the organizer record), so the default applies to every RydeFLASH case. The missing exception is silent: nothing sends an unrecorded carpool status for this service to FC-R12 or GEN-R07, unlike an unrecorded service type.
how: RydeFLASH with no is_carpool: assumed not carpool, RECORDS_MISSING, tier APPROVE (FC-R06 text, ontology note, engine, T28); the wider question (does the data carry it, what "carpool trip" means) is in D35 item 9 and O15

claim: The rule card and the engine disagree on a carpool-flagged trip of a service that has no share. FC-R06 says Ryde sets no share for RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO and Ryde+ (GEN-R07, tier HUMAN) and names only RydeSEND+carpool as undefined; the ontology note names only RYDESEND too. rider_share() applies 0.5 to any service except RydeSEND when is_carpool is True, so those services get a ruling, a refund and a driver FRAUD_SIGNAL at tier APPROVE and the RydePOOL source conflict is resolved silently (META-04 forbids that). T05 even expects RydeX+carpool to be 0.5, while Ryde's article says RydeX is 'No sharing'.
how: same as A2R2-01: a carpool flag no longer gives a no-share service the half; GEN-R07 (T29, T30)

claim: run() never sets GENERIC_ASSUMPTION_USED although META-05 requires it whenever a C or D rule or parameter is decisive. FC-F03 (C) is recorded as decisive for every detour refund and TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD (D) for the tolerance case, and the refund formula itself is FC-R08 (D); the engine_noshow tier logic sets the flag for exactly these cases. The party-facing label that tells the parties the point is a FairRyde assumption is therefore lost on every FC-R08 refund.
how: GENERIC_ASSUMPTION_USED is set when a rule rated C or D or a D parameter is decisive (engine and expectations of T09, T10, T11, T18, T24)

claim: FC-R06 and FC-F04 send an unrecorded service type to FC-R12 and the credibility note of FC-R06 says the pointers 'add no norm', but FC-R12's card does not list a missing service type (nor the engine's other FC-R12 uses: no gantry log, a gantry without a rate, a negative ERP line). The card was not updated, so the pointer extends a D rule beyond its text.
how: FC-R12 card (en and zh) lists the ERP data situations; rule_card_check pins it

claim: The description of why RydePOOL and RydeHIRE have no share is inaccurate and uses the wrong label. FC-R06 says Ryde's articles 'set no share' for RydePOOL, but the 2026 articles do set one (riders pay 50%); the real situation is a Ryde source conflict, which META-04 handles with SOURCE_CONFLICT / GEN-R-SOURCE-CONFLICT, not GEN-R07 'no written rule' (party-facing reason GEN-R-POLICY-GAP says Ryde has no rule). The conflict is not in META-04 known_conflicts. The record is also incomplete: 4408072389913 (driver, 2023-12-31) agrees with the 2026 RydePOOL text and so contradicts the other 2023 driver pages; and RydeHIRE is not 'the 2023 pages only': rider page 115000772653 (2024-04-19) says all services except RydeSEND exclude ERP, against rider page 4408072421785 (2023-04-13).
how: FC-R06 now says the pages disagree or are silent instead of "set no share"; all pages listed in the sources and notes. Moving RydePOOL and RydeHIRE to a META-04 SOURCE_CONFLICT is Jasper's choice (D35 item 7)

claim: FC-R08 says FC-R07's refund and FC-R08's refund 'together refund at most the ERP charged minus ERP(recommended)', which is false when the recommended route carries more ERP than the actual path. FC-R07 refunds charged minus ERP(actual), and the engine pays it (correctly under FC-R07), exceeding the card's stated ceiling. The en and zh sentences both overgeneralize.
how: FC-R08 en and zh: together at most the ERP charged minus the smaller of ERP(actual) and ERP(recommended); T32

claim: Open question O15 does not ask what D35 item 1 and NEXT_STEPS say it asks. D35 (1) and NEXT_STEPS attribute to O15 the open question of the ERP share for RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO and Ryde+, but O15's text covers only the carpool key-in and the split among several passengers. The question that would close the no-share services is never put to the organizer.
how: O15 now asks what D35 and NEXT_STEPS say it asks

claim: The FC-R07 zh text and the English differ at the tolerance boundary. English refunds when the ERP charged exceeds the expected ERP 'by more than' TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD (strict, as the engine does); zh says 'exceeds ... 达 TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD 以上', which means by that amount or more. The tolerance has a plausible range up to S$0.50, so the two texts give different answers when the excess equals the tolerance.
how: FC-R07 zh says "超过" (more than), as the English

claim: service_code() does not recognize the vocabulary's own labels 'Carpooling' (code CARPOOL) and 'Ryde+' (code RYDEPLUS). Both are treated as 'service type not recorded', so the reason is FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA with a false RECORDS_MISSING flag instead of share 0.5 (carpool) or GEN-R-POLICY-GAP (Ryde+). Outcome is HUMAN either way, so only the reason and flag are wrong.
how: service_code resolves the vocabulary labels (Carpooling, Ryde+); T35, T36

claim: FC-R01 uses a RydeX-only article for a general statement. how: FC-R01 also cites the all-services rider article 115000772653 and says Ryde's pages disagree for a few services

claim: D32 says FC-R08 is excluded on a metered fare for reasons 'as for FC-R00' (Ryde publishes no rule for refunding any part of a metered fare; fees follow the taxi company; payment is cash only) and in the same entry keeps FC-R07's platform-computed refund of the difference on a metered fare. Those reasons apply equally to FC-R07's refund, and the keep is the builder's reading, not recorded as Jasper's decision (his prompt covers FC-R08 only). T14 pays a S$6.00 refund on a cash RydeTAXI trip.
how: the skeptic found the reasoning for the metered exclusion recorded

claim: is_carpool=True overrides FC-R06's 'no share' services. The engine gives a carpool share of 0.5 to RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Ryde+ and OTHER (and RydeTAXI) and decides at tier AUTO, although FC-R06, FC-F04, the share-table note and D35 say these services have no share and go to GEN-R07. The ontology note for is_carpool singles out only RYDESEND ('Together with RYDESEND the share is undefined (GEN-R07)'), and no test combines is_carpool with another service.
how: same as A2R2-01

claim: The FC-R08 sentence 'together they refund at most the ERP charged minus ERP(recommended)' (and the same sentence in the zh text, and the bound given in the round 2 brief) is false when ERP(actual) is lower than ERP(recommended). The engine then refunds only FC-R07's overstatement, which is correct (the rider owes only ERP(actual)), but it exceeds charged minus ERP(recommended). Reviewers who test the bound literally will report a correct refund as over-refund.
how: same as G6

claim: service_code normalizes spelling variants against the TX-SERVICE codes only, not their labels, so two vocabulary labels do not resolve: 'Carpooling' (label of CARPOOL) and 'Ryde+' (label of RYDEPLUS). how: same as G9

claim: Test T17 ('a gantry that was not active is not counted') does not test that. With the inactive gantry wrongly counted the expected ERP becomes 6.50, the rider was charged 2.50, so the case is still UPHOLD, VALID, AUTO and the test passes.
how: T17 now charges S$6.50 for the one active S$2.50 gantry, so counting the inactive gantry changes the result

claim: Several A2 behaviors and round 1 fixes still pass the build when removed (mutation survivors). rule_card_check and erp_cases do not pin: (a) the precedence sentence in FC-F04 (the test checks only that the words 'precedence' and 'FC-R08' occur, which the unrelated sentence 'FC-R00's reasoning (D32) takes precedence over FC-R08' satisfies); (b) the AUTH-04 sentence 'If one disagreement fits both G3 and G8 ... G3 applies' (round 1 F12); (c) the RydeSEND exception in FC-R01's text (round 1 A2-F5); (d) the RECALCULATED half of fc_r01's FC-F01 check (destination_edit_accepted; R3 only changes base_fare); (e) the 'recommended route has a gantry with no rate' branch of run; (f) the guards for a missing ERP line and a missing gantry log; (g) the 'PDVL' check is a bare substring that survives deleting the 'verified for private-hire (PDVL) drivers only' sentence. how: pinned: the FC-F04 order sentence, the AUTH-04 G3-not-G8 sentence, the RydeSEND text in FC-R01, the PDVL sentence and the FC-R12 list; added a RECALCULATED fc_r01 case (R7) and a RydeSEND fc_r01 case (R8). Not added: a separate case for an unrated recommended gantry (the FC-R12 branch is covered by T16, T31 and T34)

claim: D38 (and the CW-F06 source note) record only two effects of the D34 item 1 change: such a message reads UNCLEAR, and a place plus an explicit admission also reads UNCLEAR. They omit a third, larger effect on the outcome: a message that names a listed place together with a placement or a question about the driver ('I'm at the mall entrance', 'I'm at the mall now. where r u') used to read UNCLEAR (LATE and PLACES together) and now reads PLACES, so the claim moves from UPHOLD at tier APPROVE to ESCALATE_HUMAN at tier HUMAN with F-RIDER-EVIDENCE STRONG. Safe direction and consistent with CW-F06, but it changes an outcome and tier in an in-scope type and no test pins it. (The step changed the reader, so this is not under the D34 freeze.)
how: D38 records the PLACES side effect; three reading cases

claim: The record of why Ryde X GO, Ryde+ (and RydeHIRE) have no share is one-sided. The rider article that FC-R06 itself cites, RYDE-115000772653, also says 'For all services apart from RydeSEND, ERP charges are excluded from the fares', which covers those services (edited 2024-04-19, so B, and older than the 2026 article). Neither the table note, FC-R06, FC-F04 nor D35 mentions it, yet each says 'Ryde's articles set no share for any other service'. The narrowing from the v0.1 rule (every service except RydeSEND pays) moves these services, and every FC-TOLL case without a service type, from a possible APPROVE to tier HUMAN; that is a design choice, but the record should show the sentence that argues the other way, so that Jasper decides with both.
how: the 2024 rider article RYDE-115000772653 is named in the table note, FC-R06's credibility note and D35

claim: FC-R06, FC-F04, PB-FC-TOLL and the engine send a trip with no recorded service type to FC-R12 ('insufficient data'), but FC-R12 (unchanged in A2) lists what is missing as 'the recorded distance, a usable road-matched path, the fare breakdown or the recommended route', pings, and does not name the service type or the gantry log. claim: The rule cards and the engine disagree on what opens the FC-TOLL claim when the longer route passes a gantry the recommended route also passes. claim: run() decides a case at tier AUTO (UPHOLD, FC-R-TOLL-VALID) when route_review is present but the recommended route's gantries are missing, although FC-R12 says a missing recommended route means no finding and escalation. fc_r01 treats the same input as FC-R12 (escalate), so the two functions disagree. A detour ERP claim that cannot be checked is upheld automatically.
how: route_review present without the recommended gantries is FC-R12 (T31)

claim: Booleans are taken literally: is_carpool is honored only when it is exactly True, and a gantry is skipped only when active is exactly False. A carpool trip flagged 'true', 'yes' or 1 is treated as non-carpool (full ERP charge upheld at AUTO); a gantry with active 'false', 0 or null is counted as active. fc_r01 uses truthiness instead (g.get('active', True)), so the two functions also disagree on active=None.
how: one boolean helper for is_carpool and active ("true", "yes", 1, "false", "no", 0); an unparseable is_carpool is FC-R12; T33, T38, T39

claim: The FC-R08 card says FC-R07's refund 'comes on top, so together they refund at most the ERP charged minus ERP(recommended)'. That is false whenever ERP(recommended) is higher than ERP(actual) while the path still passed a gantry the recommended route avoids (and for any overstated line on a route cheaper than the recommended one). The engine refunds the full FC-R07 difference, more than the stated cap, so the card and the engine give different amounts.
how: same as G6

claim: Non-numeric values crash the engines instead of going to FC-R12, and fc_r01 crashes on inputs that run() handles. run(): charged '' or 'abc' and a gantry rate '' raise ValueError. fc_r01: gantry_passes null raises TypeError, a gantry row without 'gantry' raises KeyError, quoted_fare 'S$19.80' raises ValueError. An empty string is what a CSV or form export writes for a missing amount.
how: one numeric helper; empty, non-numeric, NaN and infinite values go to FC-R12; fc_r01 uses the same helpers (T34)

claim: NaN and infinity pass the numeric checks: a NaN rate or NaN ERP line makes every comparison false, so the case ends UPHOLD at AUTO; an infinite line gives a refund of inf.
how: same as A2R2-05 (math.isfinite)

claim: is_metered tests 'metered' as a substring of fare_type, so 'Non-metered', 'unmetered' and 'fixed (not metered)' count as METERED. FC-F01 says RydeTAXI is METERED and every other service FIXED_AT_BOOKING. Such a trip is escalated under D32 instead of getting the FC-R08 ruling, and fc_r01 reports applies=False.
how: is_metered ignores "non-metered", "unmetered" and "not metered" (T37)

claim: Two trace and evidence gaps: (a) when an FC-R07 overstatement was found and the recommended route's rate is then unknown, the run ends ESCALATE_HUMAN with reasons ['FC-R-TOLL-OVERSTATED', 'FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA'] and the DRIVER fraud signal kept, although FC-R12 says to make no adverse finding when escalating, and erp_code_check's own rule (a reason carries its outcome) is violated; the metered branch resets reasons but this branch does not; (b) identical duplicate rows in gantry_passes are counted as two passes.
how: (a) fixed: the FC-R12 escalation clears the reasons and attaches the FC-R07 finding; (b) identical duplicate gantry rows counted twice: recorded in D35 item 6

claim: fc_r01 decides 'extra gantries' by gantry name only, while run() decides by rate and activity, so FC-R01 can fail to open the FC-TOLL claim that FC-R08 would pay, or open a pointless one. Also the gantry rate fallback ignores the UTC offset of the timestamp.
how: fc_r01 uses the same active parsing as run; the timestamp offset in the table lookup is recorded in D35 item 6

claim: FC-R07 puts the FRAUD_SIGNAL on the driver for any ERP line above expected without checking who entered it. The E11 case carries erp_toll_source ('keyed in by driver at drop-off') and the engine ignores it; an empty gantry log with an ERP line charged also yields refund plus a driver fraud signal without checking that a GPS trace exists to support 'no gantry passed'.

claim: resolve_g3 does not validate its inputs: a blind tier with a stray character or other case ('HUMAN ', 'human') counts as the lowest and is downgraded to APPROVE; an outcome 'escalate_human' in lower case is not recognized as ESCALATE_HUMAN (tier APPROVE instead of HUMAN); a blind ruling without a 'tier' key raises KeyError.
how: resolve_g3 refuses an unknown tier (ValueError) except the "n/a (reclassified...)" text

claim: AUTH-04's tie-break 'If one disagreement fits both G3 and G8 ..., G3 applies' can be read as letting G3 absorb a separate G8 disagreement: the history-blind pass against the rules engine. When the history-blind pass and the rules engine (both history-free) disagree and the history-aware pass sides with the engine, the blind ruling becomes the provisional ruling at APPROVE although it is the outlier. engine_gates has no G8 input, so the code cannot show which is meant.
how: AUTH-04 (en and zh): the history-aware or fraud-check disagreement with the history-blind pass is G3 and not G8; Judge passes among themselves or with the rules engine are G8; pinned in rule_card_check
